content: In March 2016, an afternoon in Seoul, the author watched a program they helped build place a stone on the fifth line of a Go board. The move, number 37 in game two of a five‑game match, appeared absurd, and some commentators thought it was …
summary: In March 2016 in Seoul, the author observed a Go program they helped build place a stone on the fifth line as a gift to its human opponent, with Move 37 in game two of a five‑game match appearing absurd to commentators. The author concludes that large language models do not reason.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: New competition rewards participants for lowering their biological age
content:
A new contest pits competitors against each other in a race to biological youth

The author announced that they have officially signed up for an unusual competition that rewards participants for getting younger. The competition focuses on competitors’ biological ages, which are intended to provide a better way to measure age-related changes.

The author recently turned 40 and noted that while time and chronological age only move forward, the contest’s emphasis is on biological age. No further details about the competition’s structure or prizes were provided.
summary: The author, who recently turned 40, signed up for a competition that rewards competitors for reducing their biological age. The contest focuses on biological age metrics as an alternative way to measure youth.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Hospital and radiology network blame Palantir scheduling software for errors and burnout
content:
A hospital giant and a radiology network adopted Palantir’s software to streamline their scheduling processes.  

Nurses and other staff members say the new system has introduced errors, increased burnout, and generated frustration among frontline workers.  

The criticism highlights growing concerns that the technology intended to improve efficiency is instead creating additional challenges for health‑care personnel.
summary: A hospital giant and a radiology network adopted Palantir software to streamline scheduling. Nurses and other staff say the new software is causing errors, burnout and frustration.
author: Wired

title: Patched flaw in ChatGPT Mac app could have let hackers steal sensitive data
content:
A vulnerability in the Mac version of the ChatGPT app was recently patched, highlighting a potential avenue for hackers to obtain sensitive data.  

The flaw, if exploited, could have allowed unauthorized access to user information, underscoring that AI software itself can be an inviting and vulnerable target.  

The incident comes as attention remains focused on the hacking capabilities of AI agents, reminding stakeholders that the applications powering these agents may also contain security weaknesses.
summary: A vulnerability in the ChatGPT Mac app was recently patched. The flaw could have let hackers grab sensitive data, showing AI software is an inviting and vulnerable target.
author: Wired

title: Election deniers label GOP midterm polling a psyop
content:
Election deniers have claimed that the GOP’s poor midterm polling is a “psyop.”  According to reports, dozens of high‑profile MAGA influencers and pundits have weighed in on the issue.  

Catturd posted on X that “The laughable fake polls are rolling out.”
summary: Dozens of high‑profile MAGA influencers and pundits have weighed in on the claim. Catturd posted on X that the polls are “laughable fake polls” rolling out.
author: Wired

title: Waymo, Zoox and Tesla driverless cabs have cameras pointing at riders
content:
Self‑driving cars from Waymo, Zoox, and Tesla are equipped with a network of cameras and sensors.  

The vehicles are studded with these devices, which are used to navigate and monitor the surrounding environment.  

Some of the cameras and sensors are positioned to point directly at riders.
summary: Self‑driving cars from Waymo, Zoox and Tesla are studded with cameras and sensors. Some of those cameras are aimed at the riders.
author: Wired

title: AI music platform Suno launches public beta for speech generation
content:
SunO, the AI music‑generation platform, has added a new feature that produces spoken voices from scripts or prompted descriptions. The speech capability is now available in public beta on SunO’s web and mobile platforms and can generate voiceovers and background music at the same time.

In the announcement, SunO chief product officer Jack Brody said, “Music will always be at the heart of SunO and what we build. At the same time, our vision has always extended to other forms of human expression. Today, we’re expanding what’s possible in SunO with Speech: the first audio model that generates voice and music to …”

The full story was reported by The Verge.
summary: Suno introduced a public‑beta feature that generates spoken voices from scripts or prompts, announced by chief product officer Jack Brody. The speech tool can produce voiceovers together with background music on Suno’s web and mobile platforms.
author: The Verge

title: SpaceX launches Jessica Watkins and crew to ISS after fuel leak delay
content:
SpaceX successfully launched a four‑astronaut crew to the International Space Station on Thursday, marking the start of a mission that is slated to continue until spring. The launch came after a three‑week postponement to repair a leaking fuel system in the crew capsule.

Commander Jessica Watkins, the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit, made her second trip to the space station. The crew also includes a Canadian astronaut whose wife is expected to give birth while he is away.

Thick morning clouds threatened to halt the countdown, but conditions cleared sufficiently to allow a safe liftoff. The mission proceeds under NASA’s oversight following the resolved technical issues.
summary: SpaceX lifted off commander Jessica Watkins and three other astronauts to the International Space Station on Thursday. The launch, delayed three weeks to fix a leaking fuel system, proceeded after clouds cleared and will keep the crew on the station until spring.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon AI model only to vetted cybersecurity experts
content:
Google has announced the release of its latest artificial‑intelligence model, Gemini 4 Argon, but has limited access to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts. The move is intended to prevent potential misuse of the technology by hackers.

The company said it would withhold Gemini 4 Argon from the public for now, making it available only to the selected experts. This restricted release is part of a phased approach to safely introduce frontier AI capabilities.

In a blogpost announcing the model, Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google’s chief AI architect, wrote, “Safely releasing frontier capabilities at this level requires a phased approach.”
summary: Google said it will withhold its most powerful AI model from the public and release Gemini 4 Argon only to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts. Chief AI architect Koray Kavukcuoglu said the phased approach is needed to prevent misuse by hackers.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Feeld founders receive record £3.8m dividend after 32% sales rise
content:
Feeld, the UK‑based dating platform for non‑monogamous, queer and kinky users, announced a record £3.8 million dividend for its founders after a sharp rise in sales.  

The company said revenue jumped 32 % to £64 million, with users outside the United Kingdom contributing nearly 90 % of that income. Feeld attributes the growth to “open‑minded people exploring love, desire and alternative relationships in a safe, inclusive space,” drawing users away from more mainstream rivals.  

The £3.8 million payout represents the app’s largest dividend to date, reflecting the recent surge in interest and financial performance.
summary: Feeld, a UK‑based dating app for non‑monogamous, queer and kinky users, reported revenues jumped 32% to £64 million. The growth enabled the company to pay a record £3.8 million dividend to its founders.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Lobbyist Martha Dalton helped Andy Burnham become PM via Makerfield byelection
content:
A lobbyist who recently represented the US technology firm Palantir is reported to have played a senior role in the political rise of Andy Burnham. Martha Dalton, whose consultancy Lodestone provided services to Palantir in 2024 and 2025, was involved in Burnham’s campaign during the Makerfield by‑election that returned him to parliament.

Dalton worked closely with Burnham’s team on strategic communications and rebuttals for the by‑election. After the victory, she was among the supporters who clapped Burnham into Downing Street in July.

The involvement of Dalton, a recent Palantir lobbyist, is cited as a key factor in Burnham’s successful bid to become prime minister.
summary: Martha Dalton, whose firm Lodestone worked for Palantir in 2024 and 2025, campaigned for Andy Burnham in the Makerfield byelection that secured his return to parliament. She coordinated strategic communications and rebuttals with Burnham’s team and was among supporters who clapped him into Downing Street in July.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Christa Pike in critical condition after Tennessee botched execution
content:
Christa Pike is in critical condition following a botched execution in Tennessee, her lawyer said.  

Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed 19‑year‑old Colleen Slemmer at a job‑training camp for young people.  

The lawyer confirmed Pike’s condition remains critical after the execution attempt.
summary: Pike is in critical condition following a botched execution in Tennessee, according to her lawyer. She was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed 19‑year‑old Colleen Slemmer at a job training camp for young people.
author: Euronews

title: FlyDubai captain Smit Machchhar recounts cockpit attack and fight to regain control
content:
A FlyDubai captain who helped avert a disaster is speaking publicly about the incident while recovering in hospital. Capt. Smit Machchhar described the moment he fought to regain control of the cockpit after the aircraft entered a steep descent.

The pilot said he was “fighting for his life” but knew he had to get back up to prevent a tragedy on the FlyDubai flight.
summary: Capt. Smit Machchhar is still recovering in hospital after helping prevent a tragedy on a FlyDubai flight. He said he was “fighting for his life” as he worked to regain control of the cockpit during a steep descent.
author: Euronews

title: Uzbekistan wins gold at record-breaking Chess Olympiad in Samarkand
content:
Uzbekistan captured the gold medal at the record‑breaking Chess Olympiad held in Samarkand, winning on home soil.

The tournament featured almost 400 teams representing more than 190 countries and was contested over 11 rounds.

Germany secured the bronze medal, while Hungary, France, Spain, Azerbaijan and Armenia also finished among the top ten teams.
summary: Uzbekistan captured the gold medal at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand. The competition featured almost 400 teams from more than 190 countries over 11 rounds, with Germany taking bronze and Hungary, France, Spain, Azerbaijan and Armenia finishing in the top ten.
author: Euronews

title: World's tallest wind turbine, 365 m, installed in Schipkau, Germany
content:
Germany has installed a new wind turbine that, at 365 metres tall, is the world’s tallest.

The turbine stands in Schipkau and was designed to capture stronger winds at its record height.

It is scheduled to begin operating in November.
summary: Germany’s new 365‑metre wind turbine in Schipkau is the world’s tallest. It is designed to capture stronger winds and will start operating in November.
author: Euronews

title: Houthis reject Saudi claim drone hit electricity station powering Prophet's Mosque
content:
Saudi-led coalition officials said a drone struck the Taibah electricity distribution station, which provides power to the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, one of Islam’s holiest sites.  

The coalition linked the attack to the Houthi movement, alleging the group targeted the holy site’s infrastructure.  

The Houthis rejected the allegation, calling it a “lie” intended to support previous accusations against them.
summary: The Saudi-led coalition said a drone struck the Taibah electricity distribution station that supplies power to the Prophet's Mosque in Medina. The Houthis called the allegation a "lie" and denied targeting the holy site.
author: Euronews

title: Pete Hegseth establishes Pentagon Office of Religious Affairs reporting to him
content:
Pete Hegseth has established a Pentagon Office of Religious Affairs that reports directly to him.  

Since taking the role, Hegseth has infused his evangelical Christianity into his leadership of the department, hosting worship services for employees and frequently describing the United States as a Christian nation.
summary: Pete Hegseth created a Pentagon Office of Religious Affairs that reports directly to him. He has infused his evangelical Christianity into his Pentagon leadership, hosting worship services for employees and often describing the United States as a Christian nation.
author: Euronews

title: Thousands attend secret New York Dîner en Blanc with Parisian Belle Époque theme
content:
Thousands of participants dressed in white gathered at a secret location in New York for Dîner en Blanc, the city’s annual outdoor dinner.  

The event, which celebrates a Parisian Belle Époque theme, transformed the hidden venue into a large, white‑clad gathering for the annual celebration.
summary: Thousands of participants dressed in white gathered at a secret New York location for Dîner en Blanc. The dinner is an annual outdoor event with a Parisian Belle Époque theme.
author: Euronews

title: France and Spain aim to reinforce bilateral ties as Europe's power shifts east
content:
France and Spain are working to strengthen their bilateral ties as Europe’s balance of power shifts eastward. The effort is highlighted by French President Emmanuel Macron’s recent visit to Spain, which political scientist Carlos Mascarell Vilar, based in Spain, says must be viewed through the lenses of European power, political legacy and geoeconomics.

According to Delano D’Souza, who welcomed Mascarell Vilar, the Madrid‑Paris axis is being reinforced at a time when eastern European nations such as Poland are gaining influence. Macron’s push to deepen the Franco‑Spanish partnership is presented as part of a broader strategy to advance European defence and strategic sovereignty.
summary: France and Spain are seeking to reinforce their bilateral relationship as Europe’s balance of power moves toward eastern countries such as Poland. Macron’s visit to Spain is intended to strengthen the Madrid‑Paris axis as part of a broader effort to advance European defence and strategic sovereignty.
author: France 24

title: Éric Fassin frames French student protests as demand for dignity and equal study conditions
content:
Parisian student protests have grown into a broader movement demanding “respect, dignity and decent working conditions,” according to sociologist Éric Fassin.  

Alison Sargent welcomed Fassin, a professor at Paris VIII University, who described the demonstrations as a call for equality, dignity and recognition. He noted that students from working‑class suburbs are pressing for the basic conditions that enable study and for the same opportunities enjoyed by students elsewhere.  

Fassin said the unrest, which began among students in the Parisian suburbs and has since spread, constitutes a social movement with a political and democratic dimension. He also placed the protests within a longer history of repression of social movements in France.
summary: Éric Fassin, a sociologist and professor at Paris VIII University, said the French student protests are a demand for equality, dignity and recognition. He noted that students from working‑class suburbs are seeking basic conditions that make studying possible and the same opportunities as other students, viewing the movement as a social and democratic response within a history of repression.
author: France 24

title: Bamo Nouri says US withdrawal from Iraq will boost Iran's influence
content:
America is withdrawing its military forces from Iraq, a move that experts say could shift the country’s balance of power in favor of Iran. The departure is seen as a strategic and tactical mistake that may leave Iraq more vulnerable to Iranian influence.

Erin Ogunkeye, who welcomed investigative journalist Bamo Nouri—an Honorary Research Fellow in the Department of International Politics at City Saint George's University of London—argues that the end of the American presence is a profound shift. He notes that the key issue is not whether Iraq has formally regained sovereignty, but whether it has the political cohesion, security capacity and economic independence to exercise that sovereignty. Ogunkeye points out that Tehran’s influence is already embedded within Iraq’s political parties, armed groups, economic networks and financial system, meaning its power does not depend on a conventional military presence. Removing the American counterweight could give Iran‑backed groups more room to operate, while leaving Iraq’s Kurdish region—reliant on American military, intelligence and air‑defence support—facing strategic uncertainty.

The withdrawal may intensify Iran’s role in Iraq and make the country’s attempts at political and economic reform considerably more difficult.
summary: Bamo Nouri, investigative journalist and Honorary Research Fellow at City Saint George's University of London, says the end of the American military presence in Iraq marks a profound shift in the country's balance of power. He warns that Iran’s embedded influence could expand as the US leaves, creating strategic uncertainty for the Kurdish region and hindering Iraq’s political and economic reforms.
author: France 24

title: Brazil's gun lobby backs Bolsonaro as elections approach
content:
Brazil is heading to the polls amid a debate over firearms access that could sway voters in the rural south. The issue has gained prominence as the country prepares for the upcoming elections.

Under President Jair Bolsonaro, Brazil became more heavily armed than ever before. The number of registered hunters, shooters and collectors—known by the acronym “CACs”—rose sevenfold in four years, according to the report.  

Opposition leader Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has pledged to reverse this trend, a move that has irritated the powerful gun lobby. France 24’s team in Brazil reported on the developments.
summary: Brazil is heading to elections, and the issue of firearms could influence votes, especially in the rural south. Under Bolsonaro, the number of registered hunters, shooters and collectors (CACs) increased sevenfold in four years, a trend Lula promised to reverse, irritating the powerful gun lobby.
author: France 24

title: Eritrea Cuts Diplomatic Ties with Ethiopia Over Embassy Closure
content:
Eritrea has severed all diplomatic relations with Ethiopia after Addis Ababa ordered the closure of its embassy in Asmara and declared ten Eritrean diplomats persona non grata on Thursday.  

The Ethiopian decision to expel the diplomats and shut its mission prompted the Eritrean government in Asmara to cut ties, citing the move as a breach of diplomatic protocol.  

The diplomatic fallout followed overnight blasts heard in Addis Ababa, which raised concerns that renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia could spread.
summary: Ethiopia ordered the closure of its embassy in Eritrea and declared 10 Eritrean diplomats persona non grata. In response, Asmara severed all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia after overnight blasts in Addis Ababa raised fears of renewed conflict.
author: France 24

title: Brazil Election Debate Cancelled as Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro Pull Out
content:
Brazil’s presidential race heads into the second round amid a cancelled debate

The two‑round presidential election in Brazil begins this weekend, with former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and his rival Flávio Bolsonaro facing off in a contest that has drawn intense national attention. The campaign’s final event—a scheduled presidential debate—was cancelled after both Lula and Bolsonaro pulled out, leaving the electorate without a direct face‑to‑face confrontation.

In a broader press review dated Friday, October 2, French newspapers reported on the violent turn of high‑school blockades across France, while the Brazilian election remains the focal point of international coverage. The review also noted that the finalists for this year’s Comedy Wildlife Awards have been announced, adding a cultural dimension to the weekend’s news cycle.
summary: The Brazilian two‑round presidential election begins this weekend after a campaign that ended with a cancelled debate. President Lula and rival Flavio Bolsonaro both withdrew from the debate.
author: France 24

title: EU fully rejects US threat to ban diesel exports unless fuel stocks released
content:
The European Union on Friday “fully” rejected a United States threat to ban diesel exports unless the bloc releases additional fuel stocks, an EU official said.

The official’s statement emphasized that the EU pushes back against the proposed ban and will not comply with the demand to increase fuel stock releases.
summary: The European Union on Friday pushed back against a US threat to ban any diesel exports unless the bloc releases more of its fuel stocks. An EU official said the EU “fully” rejected the move.
author: France 24

title: Refugee education funding cuts threaten millions, teenage Sudanese girl seeks tech degree
content:
I have not lost my dreams: Refugee education funding cuts threaten millions

A teenage girl who fled war‑torn Sudan for neighbouring Egypt and hopes to pursue a technology degree is an example of why countries must ensure that young refugees can continue to learn. The story illustrates the broader impact of cuts to refugee education funding, which threaten the educational prospects of millions of displaced youth.
summary: A teenage girl who fled war‑torn Sudan to Egypt hopes to pursue a technology degree. Her story illustrates how refugee education funding cuts threaten millions of young refugees.
author: UN News

title: Cairo strips 66‑metre Tutankhamun and Nefertiti mural before Xi Jinping visit
content:
A row erupted in Cairo after city authorities removed a 66‑metre‑long mural depicting Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti from view on the eve of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit. The painting, which was part of a set of 40 murals commissioned to beautify the city for the visit, was created by the volunteer youth group Rasmet Basma in Tahrir Square.

The mural was removed because it allegedly revived Afrocentric claims about the origins of the pharaohs, a controversy that prompted the authorities to act before the president’s arrival. The removal was carried out to keep the mural out of the esteemed guest’s line of sight.
summary: City authorities removed a 66‑metre mural depicting Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti with dark skin, painted by volunteer youth group Rasmet Basma in Tahrir Square. The mural was one of 40 commissioned to beautify Cairo for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit and was taken down amid allegations it revived Afrocentric claims about the pharaohs’ origins.
author: Guardian World

title: Manchester City to launch appeal as financial breach fallout expands
content:
Manchester City will launch an appeal as the legal fallout from alleged financial breaches expands.  

The club’s appeal comes amid a widening legal dispute that now extends beyond the Premier League case.  

A deadline is set for Friday, underscoring the urgency of the proceedings.
summary: Manchester City plans to launch an appeal over the alleged financial breaches. A Friday deadline approaches as the legal fallout widens beyond the Premier League case.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Arab party leader Sami Abu Shehadeh forced to withdraw from Israeli Knesset election
content:
The upcoming Knesset vote has seen Palestinian participation shrink as Arab party leader Sami Abu Shehadeh withdrew from the elections.

Abu Shehadeh’s withdrawal has been reported as a forced exit, further reducing the number of Palestinian representatives in the Israeli legislature.
summary: Sami Abu Shehadeh was forced to withdraw from the upcoming Knesset election. His withdrawal reduces Palestinian participation in the vote.
author: Al Jazeera

title: NBA shuts only Africa training academy, shifts focus to Abu Dhabi global academy
content:
The National Basketball Association (NBA) announced the closure of its sole training academy in Africa, a move that has disappointed young players in the region.  

In a statement, the NBA said its focus is now on a new global academy that will open in Abu Dhabi. The announcement comes amid closures of NBA training facilities in Mexico and Australia.
summary: The NBA has closed its sole training academy in Africa. The league said its focus is now on a new global academy opening in Abu Dhabi as academies in Africa, Mexico and Australia are also being closed.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Three US aircraft carriers and two amphibious groups to position near Iran by end of November
content:
New aircraft carrier, 10,000 US troops: Is the Iran war about to escalate?

By the end of November, three U.S. aircraft carriers and two amphibious landing groups will be positioned near Iran. The deployment reflects the United States' ongoing military presence in the region. No additional actions or troop numbers are indicated in the available information.
summary: By the end of November, three US aircraft carriers will be positioned near Iran. Two amphibious landing groups will also be positioned near Iran.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Protesters disrupt Ireland-Austria football match with Palestine flags and tennis balls
content: Protesters disrupted a football match between Ireland and Austria, interrupting play with a display that included tennis balls and Palestine flags. The demonstration took place during the Ireland‑Austria game, with participants throwing the tennis balls onto the field while waving the flags.
summary: Protesters interrupted Ireland’s football match against Austria. They threw tennis balls and displayed Palestine flags during the disruption.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Shoko Kawata, Japan's first mayor on maternity leave, joins TIME100 Next list
content:
Shoko Kawata, Japan’s first mayor to take maternity leave, has been named to the TIME100 Next list. Her inclusion highlights the historic nature of her decision to step away from municipal duties while expecting a child.

Kawata’s leave sparked mixed reactions across Japan, a nation currently grappling with efforts to raise its birth rate. The public response reflects the broader debate over work‑life balance and family policies in the country.
summary: Shoko Kawata became Japan's first mayor to take maternity leave and was named to the TIME100 Next list. Her leave drew mixed reactions in Japan, a country struggling to lift birth rates.
author: BBC World

title: Cornell campus tension palpable as 2024 allegations resurface, students say
content:
Students at Cornell University told the BBC that a “dark cloud” and a “dismal” mood now hang over the campus. They said the tension on campus has become palpable.

The atmosphere, according to the students, has worsened since allegations from 2024 resurfaced, heightening unease among the university community.
summary: Students told the BBC that the tension on Cornell's campus has become palpable. The tension has increased since allegations from 2024 resurfaced.
author: BBC World

title: Flydubai pilot Capt Smit Machchhar says he opened cockpit door during co‑pilot attack
content: Flydubai pilot Capt Smit Machchhar recounted a cockpit attack by the co‑pilot, saying he intervened to prevent further casualties. The captain told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi that he opened the cockpit door to allow other crew members inside during the incident.
summary: Capt Smit Machchhar, the pilot of a Flydubai flight, described a cockpit attack by the co‑pilot. He told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi that he opened the cockpit door to let others in during the attack.
author: BBC World

title: Pelosi cancels Cornell event amid campus rape investigation
content:
Nancy Pelosi, the House Speaker Emerita, has canceled an upcoming event that was scheduled to take place on October 15 in New York City. The event was affiliated with Cornell University.

The cancellation follows fresh scrutiny of how Cornell handled a 2024 allegation of gang rape on its campus. A source close to Pelosi told The Hill that the decision to cancel came amid this investigation.
summary: House Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) canceled an upcoming event with Cornell University scheduled for Oct. 15 in New York City. The cancellation followed fresh scrutiny of the university's handling of a 2024 allegation of gang rape on its campus.
author: The Hill

title: Hochul Appoints Letitia James as Special Prosecutor in Cornell Sexual Assault Case
content:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul (D) announced Thursday evening that she has appointed state Attorney General Letitia James (D) as special prosecutor to investigate a former Cornell University student’s allegations that she was raped at a fraternity house near the Ivy League’s campus in October 2024.

The governor said the appointment was made to lead the investigation into the alleged assault. She shared the announcement in a statement posted on social media.
summary: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) announced Thursday evening that state Attorney General Letitia James (D) has been appointed as special prosecutor to investigate a former Cornell University student’s allegations that she was raped at a fraternity house near the Ivy League’s campus in October 2024. The governor said the appointment in a statement shared on social media.
author: The Hill

title: DOJ Accuses UCLA Law School of Using Race in Admissions
content:
The Department of Justice (DOJ) announced on Thursday that it has accused the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) law school of discriminating against white and Asian applicants in its admissions process.  

The DOJ said the Trump administration has also raised similar concerns about UCLA’s medical school and the law schools at Duke University and another unnamed institution.
summary: The Department of Justice accused UCLA law school of discriminating against white and Asian students in its admissions process. The Trump administration has made similar allegations against UCLA’s medical school and the law schools at Duke University.
author: The Hill

title: Trump calls Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton a 'pain in the ass' and 'controversial'
content:
President Trump made remarks about Texas Senate GOP candidate Ken Paxton during several stops in the Lone Star State and Oklahoma.  

During the tour, Trump called Paxton “a pain in the ass” and noted that he was “a little controversial.”  

The comments were unusual because Paxton is one of Trump’s endorsed candidates, and the remarks came just weeks before the November elections.
summary: President Trump called Texas Senate GOP candidate Ken Paxton a “pain in the ass” and “a little controversial” during stops in Texas and Oklahoma. He made the remarks weeks before the November elections.
author: The Hill

title: Government proposes ending £104 parent‑child seat charge on flights
content:
The government is considering a proposal to end charges that require parents to pay extra to sit next to their children on airline flights.  

According to the government, the current policy can cost a parent and child up to £104 for a return journey.
summary: The government is moving to end charges for parents to sit with their children on flights. It says the current cost for a parent and child to sit together can be up to £104 on a return journey.
author: BBC Politics

title: Increased air pollution linked to more night-time coughing, UK‑led study finds
content:
New research led by the University of Cambridge has found that increased air pollution is associated with more frequent night-time coughing, which can disrupt sleep. The study, led by Prof Cecilia Mascolo, highlights that while most air pollution research focuses on severe symptoms requiring medical attention, day-to-day effects are often overlooked.

Prof Mascolo, who hails from a highly polluted area in Italy, noted the significance of these understudied impacts. She stated, “I come from an area in Italy with very high pollution and I am very aware of its not-talked-about effects.” The findings suggest that the link between harmful emissions and sleep disturbance is a critical aspect of air pollution research.
summary: A UK‑led study found that higher air pollution levels are linked to increased night‑time coughing and disrupted sleep. Researchers noted that day‑to‑day symptoms of pollution are often overlooked and the study was led by Prof Cecilia Mascolo of the University of Cambridge.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Japan team transplants human pituitary tissue into primate, boosting cortisol
content:
Researchers in Japan have transplanted pituitary tissue grown from human stem cells into a primate that had its pituitary gland surgically removed, boosting the animal’s cortisol levels. The transplant successfully restored critical hormone signals.

The study was led by researchers from Nagoya University in Japan. In addition to the primate experiment, the team demonstrated that the same method worked in mice over a longer period.
summary: Researchers in Japan transplanted pituitary tissue grown from human stem cells into a primate whose pituitary gland had been surgically removed, restoring critical hormone signals. The team from Nagoya University also demonstrated that the same approach worked in mice over a longer period.
author: Medical Xpress

title: First clitoral reconstruction surgery developed for vulvar cancer patients
content:
A new clitoral reconstruction procedure has been developed for women who lose part of their clitoris due to vulvar cancer. This surgical technique marks the first time such a reconstruction has been created, arriving 40 years after the introduction of the first penile reconstruction surgery.

Initial results for the first group of patients treated with this procedure are encouraging.
summary: A clitoral reconstruction procedure has been developed for the first time for women who lose part of their clitoris because of vulvar cancer. Results in the initial group of patients are encouraging, 40 years after the first penile reconstruction surgery.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Metal-organic interactions key to carbon cycling, improving climate change predictions
content:
Metal‑organic interactions have been identified as a key factor in carbon cycling, potentially improving predictions of carbon dynamics under climate change.  

The global annual amount of carbon dioxide (CO₂) released through microbial decomposition of soil organic carbon is estimated to be roughly five times greater than anthropogenic CO₂ emissions.  

This disparity underscores the importance of understanding how climate change influences soil CO₂ release dynamics.
summary: The global annual amount of CO₂ released through microbial decomposition of soil organic carbon is estimated to be about five times greater than anthropogenic CO₂ emissions. This highlights the importance of understanding how climate change affects soil CO₂ release dynamics.
author: Phys.org

title: GRAPES-3 muon telescope finds thunderclouds generate extreme potentials and explains detection bias
content:
A team using the GRAPES‑3 muon telescope, originally designed to study cosmic rays, has discovered that thunderclouds can generate electrical potential differences larger than any direct measurement has recorded. The instrument’s observations revealed a surprising asymmetry: it detected many more thunderstorm events in the eastern portion of its field of view than in the western portion.

The new study, published in the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics, explains the cause of this imbalance. The research confirms that the GRAPES‑3 telescope is a powerful tool for probing the intense electric fields that develop inside thunderstorms.
summary: An instrument built to study cosmic rays, the GRAPES-3 muon telescope, has shown that thunderclouds can develop electrical potential differences far greater than those ever measured directly. The study also explains why the telescope detected many more thunderstorm events in the eastern part of its field of view than in the western part.
author: Phys.org

title: Underwater Umbrellas Could Shield Coral Reefs from Heat Damage
content: High sea temperatures driven by the climate crisis damage corals, bleaching them ghostly white and killing them. While restoration of dead reefs is possible, it is difficult and expensive, and restored corals remain vulnerable to future heat waves. Finding ways to stop or slow the damage to existing reefs is crucial.
summary: High sea temperatures cause coral bleaching and death. Restoration is expensive and vulnerable to future heat waves, so protecting existing reefs is crucial.
author: Phys.org

title: NASA Announces Free, On-Demand Movie Night for All
content:
NASA is inviting viewers to a free, on‑demand movie night featuring NASA+ documentaries. The event emphasizes NASA’s mission to pioneer the future in space exploration and scientific discovery, allowing audiences to “come along for the ride” without needing a subscription.

The lineup includes titles such as “Other Worlds: Europa,” “Cosmic Dawn,” and “Planetary,” offering a variety of space‑focused content. Viewers can watch the programming at their convenience, with no cost or subscription required.

Participants are encouraged to grab popcorn and join the journey into space science through the available documentaries.
summary: NASA is hosting a free, on-demand movie night featuring NASA+ documentaries. The event requires no subscription and invites viewers to enjoy the films with popcorn.
author: NASA News

content:

title: California law fines robotaxi operators for blocking first responders
content: A new California law imposes additional regulations on operators of autonomous vehicles. The legislation specifically targets robotaxi providers, stating that they will be subject to fines if they block first responders. The measure is intended to ensure that emergency personnel can access scenes without obstruction from self‑driving ride‑share services.
summary: A new California law imposes rules on autonomous vehicle operators. The law permits fines for robotaxi operators who block first responders.
author: TechCrunch

title: Brazil launches probe into alleged Trump administration plan to fund far‑right causes
content:
Brazil has opened an investigation into an alleged plan by the Trump administration to fund far‑right groups in the country.  

The probe is unfolding as former president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and senator Flavio Bolsonaro gear up to face each other in what observers describe as a consequential Brazilian election. The contest is seen as potentially shaping the nation’s economic outlook for decades.
summary: Brazil has opened an investigation into an alleged Trump administration scheme to finance far‑right groups in the country. The probe comes as Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro prepare to face each other in a consequential Brazilian election.
author: Euronews

title: Medical helicopter crash on Catalina Island kills pilot, nurse; two injured, one missing
content:
A medical helicopter crashed on Catalina Island in California, leaving two people dead, two injured and one still missing. The operator of the aircraft said the fatalities were its own staff members: the pilot and an onboard nurse.

Transport safety officials confirmed that an investigation into the crash is ongoing. The two injured individuals were taken to hospital, while authorities continue to search for the missing person.
summary: A medical helicopter crashed on California's Catalina Island, killing the pilot and an onboard nurse, who were staff members of the operator. Two other people were hospitalized and one remains missing while transport safety officials continue the investigation.
author: Euronews

title: Marco Rubio clears $320 million Egypt military aid withheld over human rights concerns
content:
U.S. Senator Marco Rubio approved a waiver that releases $320 million in military aid to Egypt that had been withheld because of human‑rights concerns. The waiver clears the funds for delivery while keeping the issue on the diplomatic agenda.

Rubio said Washington’s concerns about Egypt’s human‑rights record will continue to be addressed in broader bilateral discussions between the two countries.
summary: Top US diplomat Marco Rubio signed a waiver that unblocked $320 million in military aid to Egypt that had been withheld over human rights concerns. He said Washington’s concerns about Egypt’s human‑rights record will continue to be discussed in full bilateral talks.
author: Euronews

title: ICE issues guidance tightening vehicle stop rules and banning high‑speed chases
content:
New ICE guidance announced in a memo tightens rules for vehicle stops and bans officers from conducting high‑speed chases.  

The guidance was issued as the Trump administration faces mounting criticism over a series of deadly incidents involving ICE officers.  

ICE officials downplayed the measures, describing them as “mere reminders” and stating that existing protocols will continue.
summary: ICE released new guidance that tightens rules for vehicle stops and bans officers from conducting high‑speed chases. The agency said the measures are merely reminders and that existing protocols will remain in place despite criticism of recent deadly incidents involving ICE officers.
author: Euronews

title: G20 trade ministers deadlocked on industrial overcapacity, US trade chief says
content:
G20 trade ministers were unable to reach an agreement on how to address excess industrial capacity and the removal of forced labour from supply chains, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Thursday.

Speaking at the G20 talks in Milwaukee, Greer highlighted the overcapacity issue, a criticism that is often directed at China, which has rejected the claim. He also noted the lack of consensus on eliminating forced labour from global supply chains.

The United States, which holds this year’s rotating G20 presidency, said the deadlock underscores the challenges facing the group.
summary: G20 trade ministers failed to reach agreement on tackling excess industrial capacity and eliminating forced labour from supply chains, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Thursday. Greer made the remarks during talks in Milwaukee, and the United States holds this year's rotating G20 presidency.
author: France 24

title: EU monitor reports record 52% of Europe faced intense heat stress this summer
content:
A record 52% of Europe experienced intense heat stress this summer, the EU’s climate monitor reported on Friday.  

The monitor linked the widespread heatwaves to climate change and noted tens of thousands of excess deaths across the continent. Europe recorded its third‑warmest summer on record, while western Europe saw its hottest conditions, with several nations breaking national temperature records.  

The findings highlight the extent of heat stress that affected more than half of the European region this summer.
summary: A record 52% of Europe faced intense heat stress this summer, according to the EU’s climate monitor on Friday. Europe experienced its third warmest summer overall and its hottest summer in western Europe, with several countries setting national temperature records.
author: France 24

title: Saudi-led coalition says Houthis hit Medina power station serving Prophet's Mosque
content:
The Saudi‑led coalition said on Thursday that Yemen’s Iran‑backed Houthis struck an electricity distribution station that supplies the Prophet’s Mosque in the holy Saudi city of Medina.  

The coalition’s statement said the drone attack drew condemnation across the Muslim world.  

The Houthis denied involvement in the strike, which occurred as fighting intensified between Yemen’s government forces and rebels.
summary: The Saudi-led coalition said Yemen’s Iran‑backed Houthis struck an electricity distribution station that supplies the Prophet’s Mosque in Medina. The Houthis denied involvement in the drone attack as fighting intensified between government forces and rebels in Yemen, prompting condemnation across the Muslim world.
author: France 24

title: Latvia votes on Oct. 3 amid security concerns and debate over cutting ties with Russia
content:
Latvians will go to the polls on October 3 to elect a new parliament, with Russia featuring prominently in the campaign, the title notes.  

Security concerns dominate the election agenda, while a debate also unfolds over the economic cost of severing ties with Moscow, according to the source.
summary: Latvians will vote for a new parliament on October 3. The campaign is dominated by security fears and a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.
author: DW World

title: EU ministers consider return hubs and stronger Frontex, Greece eyes asylum suspension
content:
EU ministers are discussing new measures aimed at curbing irregular migration, according to recent proposals.  

The plans call for the establishment of “return hubs” outside the European Union and for a strengthening of the EU border agency Frontex. Greece has also suggested that, in emergency situations, asylum applications be temporarily suspended.  

These proposals illustrate the ministers’ focus on tightening migration controls within the bloc.
summary: EU ministers are considering proposals that include setting up return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.
author: DW World

title: Turkey stock scandal affects half a million, prompts arrests and AKP resignation
content:
Turkey’s stock market manipulation scandal has impacted nearly half a million investors, according to recent reports.

Police have carried out several arrests in connection with the scheme, and a female politician from the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) has resigned amid the fallout.

The developments highlight the scale of the alleged fraud and the political repercussions it has triggered.
summary: Nearly half a million investors have been affected by a stock market manipulation scandal in Turkey. Police have made several arrests and a female ruling‑party (AKP) politician has resigned.
author: DW World
